ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory and documented PEP screening of all General Partners, Limited Partners, and Ultimate Beneficial Owners under Article 3.5 of CSSF Regulation 12-02 and the Law of 12 November 2004. Automated screening against Luxembourg Ministry of Finance consolidated lists, UN Security Council sanctions, EU restrictive measures, and OFAC SDN/Consolidated Non-SDN Lists. Positive PEP hits trigger Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD), independent of the 25% ownership threshold; negative news institutional-risk reviews are required for all directors and natural persons with appointing influence; evidence of sanctions clearance must be retained for a minimum of 10 years from the termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official statutory name language must be expressed in Latin script. The RCS filing language is French; therefore any corporate name submitted in another language must be accompanied by an accurate French transliteration/translation adopted in the articles of association. The use of diacritical marks is permitted. Foreign-script legal names must be fully transliterated into the Latin alphabet at the moment of incorporation; no subsequent ad-hoc transliteration deviation is allowed in registry documents. The name must be capable of being pronounced and identified on French-medium registry search records. The RCS algorithm will match phonetically equivalent names against existing registrations; identical homophones are rejected.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Médical (when falsely implying licensed clinical practice)
Lux / Luxembourgeois (when implying sovereignty or state affiliation)
Titre (Title, implying a regulated securities business)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Filing is performed request-first through the RCS online 'N-name search and reservation' module; the RCS reserves the name for an initial 30-day period, renewable once at the discretion of the registry, provided a valid reason is submitted and the name remains available. Upon statutory refusal, the applicant may file a formal administrative appeal within 15 days under the general provisions of the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies and the Luxembourg Code of Administrative Procedure. A written submission must address each refusal ground, including an explanation that the name is not contrary to public order, morality, or the 'unjustified deception' doctrine under Article 15-1 of the Law of 10 August 1915. In the event of rejection after internal review, a further appeal de recours objectif may be lodged with the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within 60 days of notification. Each request requires payment of the applicable fees and supporting evidence of the legal entity's lawful purpose.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual registered-office services are permissible for a non-regulated SCSp used as a pure holding and financing vehicle, provided that the virtual office service provider has a physical presence in Luxembourg, receives and dispatches mail in accordance with the RCS rules, and permanently maintains the statutory seat as a domicile address registered with the Luxembourg Business Registers. No mailbox-only setup will satisfy the 'commercial substance' expectation under the RBE and NAVR rules if the entity carries out actual thermoplastic aligner manufacturing, intra-EEA product distribution, or invoicing activities. SSE indicators will then require a local operational decision centre, full bookkeeping records, board minutes, and substance in the form of employees or credible management functions. For a purely passive holding SCSp at the top of a dental-aligner manufacturing group, the virtual office may satisfy the registered statutory seat, but the tax consolidation and VAT treatment matter must be reviewed; the risk of qualification as 'fiction' under Circular LIR No. 56 is materially elevated. The acceptability is therefore conditional and fact-specific; a true virtual office for an operational medical-device business is not permitted.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, including the special limited partnership (SCSp) provisions introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016; Articles 916-1 et seq. and applicable partnership-law sections.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), under the supervisory authority of the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif / partnership agreement and the RCS electronic constitution filing form for a Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp), followed by publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: There is no statutory minimum subscription or paid-in capital for an SCSp. Partners freely determine capital commitments in the partnership agreement. Luxembourg law does not require a bank-escrowed or blocked account for formation, but the partnership agreement may impose payment conditions and the manager must maintain a capital contribution register for AML and accounting purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: We, the general partner of the Luxembourg SCSp, acting under the amended Law of 10 August 1915 and the SCSp provisions, adopt this first governing resolution. 1. The appended capital subscription schedule is approved as the binding commitment register. 2. The registered office is fixed at the address recorded in the partnership agreement for service of process. 3. [Manager Name] is appointed manager with authority to open bank accounts, hire staff, execute leases, and file regulatory applications. 4. The manager must complete all industrial, environmental and licensing formalities for the dental clear-aligner sheet facility. Done at Luxembourg.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name availability check and proposed profile clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS e-Processing window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Query the RCS commercial register for identical or confusing corporate names. Submit a preliminary notice identifying the legal form as SCSp, the general partner, the registered office municipality and the intended industrial activity under ISIC 3250. Obtain a written name clearance note where available and verify that the proposed name is not contrary to Luxembourg public order or reserved for regulated professions.
required_dossiers: Identity document of the general partner
Statement of intended activity covering thermoforming and trimming of dental clear-aligner sheets
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the proposed name, revise the name and resubmit. A final refusal may be challenged before the Administrative Tribunal within three months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the SCSp constitutive deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary or qualified legal counsel; the RCS accepts a notarized deed or a private deed where the partnership agreement satisfies formal publication requirements
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the SCSp partnership agreement containing the corporate purpose, capital commitment schedule, profit and loss allocation, management powers, transfer restrictions, liquidation clauses and governing law. Obtain the written consent of the owner or management company of the registered office address. Execute the deed before a notary if the governance structure requires notarization.
required_dossiers: Register of partners and capital commitments
Identity and power-of-attorney documents for signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct and re-execute the document promptly; purely typographical corrections may be made by addendum without triggering a new public filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the SCSp constitution application electronically together with the constitutive deed and all required declarations. Pay the RCS registration fee. The RCS will assign the national business number and cause the publication of the constitution extract in RESA. After publication, obtain the official RCS excerpt proving the validity of the SCSp vis-à-vis third parties.
required_dossiers: Partners list and general partner consent
Proof of payment of the registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query, submit the requested supplementary documents through the same e-filing channel. Refusal of registration may be appealed to the Administrative Tribunal within three months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the RCS excerpt to activate the Luxembourg national business number for direct tax purposes. Register for VAT with the AEDT and, if the SCSp has no Luxembourg establishment, appoint a VAT representative. Submit the partnership transparency declaration for direct tax classification and register any employees with the CCSS for social security and employer withholding.
required_dossiers: VAT registration form and manager identity documents
Employee registration and social security declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Single Point of Contact coordinates between administrations; cure any deficiency notice within one month or request an extension in writing before the statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction générale de l'industrie; filing through the Luxembourg Guichet Unique pour Entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Luxembourg business establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) covering industrial thermoforming and automated trimming of multilayer polymer sheets for dental aligners. Demonstrate that the manager meets professional qualification requirements, submit a clean criminal record certificate, and describe the production site, machinery and quality-control processes.
required_dossiers: Criminal record extract for the manager
Description of production equipment and process flow
Site plan and floor space declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to the Ministry with supplementary evidence and, if necessary, attend an administrative hearing. Refusal or conditional authorization may be challenged before the Administrative Tribunal within three months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental screening and integrated environmental permit
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a preliminary environmental screening to determine whether the thermoforming and trimming installation is classified as a classed installation requiring an integrated environmental authorization under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental permits. If thresholds are exceeded, prepare an environmental impact assessment report and conduct the public consultation procedure. Include monitoring commitments for air emissions, wastewater, noise and production waste.
required_dossiers: Environmental screening form or full EIA report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The applicant must answer all supplementary information requests within the procedural time limits. A final refusal may be appealed to the Administrative Tribunal; interim operation can be requested only after obtaining an urgent suspension order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Fire safety, structural control and occupational clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); Corps grand-ducal et communal de lutte contre l'incendie et de secours (CGDIS); municipal building authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the municipal building or occupation permit for the industrial unit. Engage an approved technical control office to certify the structural load capacity of floors supporting trimming and thermoforming machines. Apply for the CGDIS fire-safety clearance by submitting the fire-protection concept, evacuation routes and fire-suppression measures. Register the workplace with ITM and arrange mandatory occupational health surveillance.
required_dossiers: Occupational health service registration and medical surveillance program
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Remedial works may be imposed by the commune or CGDIS. Submit a phased compliance plan and, where necessary, challenge the permit conditions before the Administrative Tribunal while maintaining safe operational shutdown measures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction générale de l'industrie, des nouvelles technologies et de la recherche; Ministère de la Santé - Direction de la Santé for medical-device establishment matters; Administration de l'Environnement for environmental permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement industrielle and integrated environmental authorization (autorisation environnementale intégrée); additionally, a health-establishment registration/permit for the manufacture of dental clear-aligner sheets as medical devices under Luxembourg law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency), under the authority of the Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Classed installation under the Grand-Ducal regulation on environmental authorizations of 2 March 2018. Mandatory preliminary EIA screening applies to thermoforming and polymer-sheet processing. A full EIA report is required where installed production capacity or solvent consumption exceeds the thresholds set out in the annexes; otherwise a simplified environmental notification and integrated permit application will be processed.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to public sewer must comply with the municipal wastewater regulation; pH must remain within 6.5 to 9.5, COD not exceed 125 mg/L, BOD5 not exceed 25 mg/L and TSS not exceed 35 mg/L. Air extraction from thermoforming and trimming lines must be captured so that solvent and VOC concentrations comply with Directive 2010/75/EU; fugitive VOC emissions must be controlled below occupational and environmental limit values, and production waste must be segregated under European waste codes and dispatched to authorised recovery facilities with full consignment documentation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required from CGDIS, including proof of smoke extraction, emergency exits, fire extinguishing systems and evacuation planning. Structural load inspection by an approved technical control office is mandatory for all plant floors. ITM occupational clearance requires a written workplace risk assessment, personal protective equipment provisions and an occupational health surveillance system for all employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) / Administration des contributions directes (ACD); e-portal: MyGuichet.lu (https://guichet.public.lu) and the AEDT e-space (https://paiement.etat.lu / eTVA)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) File business incorporation with Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via notary/practitioner on MyGuichet.lu to obtain the 11-digit national business/company registration number (numéro d'immatriculation). 2) Register for VAT by filing Form 640 (immatriculation à la TVA) with the AEDT for non-established taxable persons, or Form 640b / standard registration for the SCSp; the AEDT issues the 14-character VAT number prefix 'LU'. 3) SCSp also obtains an EORI number for customs purposes. 4) Foreign entities without local permanent establishment must appoint a Luxembourg tax representative (représentant fiscal) for the VAT/customs procedure if required by AEDT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box'. Under Art. 175 LIR the SCSp is fiscally transparent (pass-through) by default; Art. 165 LIR permits an irrevocable option for the partnership to become subject to corporate income tax (opaque status) when specific conditions are met. For VAT, the SCSp is a distinct taxable person under Art. 4 of the VAT Law, allowing the partnership to hold its own VAT/EORI registration even while income-tax-transparent; hybrid mismatch rules (ATAD) apply to deny benefits where the same payment is deductible in Luxembourg and non-taxable abroad.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (VAT / TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover local small-business franchise (Art. 57 VAT Law) for Luxembourg-established businesses; zero threshold for non-established foreign suppliers and for intra-EU distance selling unless the EUR 10,000 OSS Union scheme threshold is met; EUR 100,000 was replaced for goods distance selling by the EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold since 1 July 2021
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no digital stamping ('validation') regime. Mandatory B2G e-invoicing via Peppol BIS 3.0 (and/or PEPPOL-compliant format) since 1 January 2021 for invoices to Luxembourg public entities. B2B e-invoicing is optional; AEDT accepts EDI/Peppol/structured XML on request. Invoice archiving mandatory for 10 years; per-article tax records must support deductibility and zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to the supply/export of dental-clear-aligner sheets (multilayer thermoformable sheets) when (i) the goods are dispatched/transported from Luxembourg to a destination outside the EU, (ii) the exporter holds an accepted export customs declaration (SAD/ENS) and transport documentation (CMR, bill of lading or air waybill) proving departure from EU customs territory within 90 days of supply, and (iii) the confirmatory report from the customs office (visa de sortie) is obtained within the legal timeframe. Intra-EU supplies can be zero-rated only if the customer's valid EU VAT number is evidenced in the EC Sales List/VIES and the invoice is issued by the 15th day of the month following the supply; services ancillary to the export (freight, handling) are zero-rated to non-EU recipients.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/ENS, via LU customs gateway)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR (proof of departure from EU)
Commercial Invoice with Incoterms and export zero-rating annotation
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank transfer proof (SWIFT MT103 or card settlement record evidencing cross-border payment)
EC Sales List / Recapitulative Statement (for intra-EU supplies) and customer VAT number validation record

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (Central Bank of Luxembourg) in conjunction with the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the banking prudential and FX administration authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies the euro as legal tender and full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions by virtue of EU Treaty arts. 63–65 TFEU. Profit remittance, loan repayments, and dividend-like distributions to non-resident partners are unrestricted; there is no exchange licensing requirement, but bank documentation and CRS/FATCA declarations are mandatory. The AMLA-driven compliance framework requires the SCSp to identify the unlimited partner and the economically beneficial owner for any repatriation flow.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg does not impose any mandatory surrender of export proceeds, any statutory conversion ratio, or an inward remittance timeline. Exporters (including the clear aligner sheet manufacturer) may retain foreign currency in licensed bank accounts or convert freely through authorized intermediaries subject to BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational EUR Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational EUR Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational EUR Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational EUR Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility as an auxiliary banking vector for platform-driven card settlements (e.g., Stripe/Adyen, Wirecard, Payoneer) and for daily trade disbursements; low feasibility as the sole treasury rail for high-value international trade. A licensed EU EMI/PI may provide virtual IBANs and onward SWIFT/SEPA execution, but cannot extend bank guarantees, hold settlement balances above fallback thresholds, or replace a regulated Luxembourg credit institution for documentary collections and letters of credit. The EMI must itself be regulated under PSD2 and maintain a correspondence account with a tier-1 bank inside SEPA.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors are not statutorily required to appear physically in Luxembourg for an SCSp bank account; however, tier-1 banks will generally mandate a virtual or physical KYC interview with at least the registered managing partner or a locally authorized delegate. Remote video identification is accepted in compliance with CSSF circular 12/552 if, inter alia, the SCSp has no negative press, a transparent responsible partner, and a compliant registered office. For high-risk or opaque ownership, in-person attendance in Luxembourg City is normally demanded.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership of the SCSp, especially where the limited partner is a foreign trust or an unregulated holding vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified extract from the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), the partnership deed and management agreement, a signed ownership-chain spreadsheet, passport copies of every partner holding more than 10%, and a formal legal opinion on the SCSp's transparency issued by a Luxembourg law firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of initial capital contribution being cross-border or non-European, raising anti-money-laundering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Produce audited financial statements of the contributor, six months of bank reference statements from a regulated financial institution, evidence of the economic purpose of the injection (purchase of thermoforming machinery/raw materials), tax identification numbers, and a notarised capital commitment certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual trade activity for the stated dental clear aligner manufacturing scope, such as high turnover without physical goods or large dealings with high-risk jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Attach ISO 13485/GMP certificates and manufacturing agreements, commercial contracts or purchase orders underlying each material flow, shipping/incoterm documents, and copies of invoices tied to the aligner sheet production. In addition, file a business plan and cash-flow forecast demonstrating that receivables from dental distributors are consistent with the manufacturing cycle.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant route is SEPA Credit Transfer for euro contributions under EUR 100k, and SWIFT MT103 for higher-value injections; beneficiary should be the SCSp's operating account at a Luxembourg bank. The wire instruction must reference the SCSp's RCS number, the country of origin, and the European balance-of-payments direct-investment classification 'Equity capital in non-listed enterprise' to ease BCL statistical reporting. The receiving bank must obtain an updated UBO declaration, an executed capital commitment schedule, and prior notification of the injection if the amount exceeds the bank's internal threshold. Foreign-currency injections may be converted to euros on the spot market by the receiving bank; no prior central bank approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade payments for raw materials (PETG/PU sheets) and components should use SWIFT MT103/MT202 for wire transfers; for equipment purchases, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit payable at sight (UCP 600) is the standard rail. Exports of dental clear aligner sheets to EU distributors are cleared through SEPA Instant under IBAN collection; non-EU sales via MT103 or documentary collection. All disbursements require invoice and commercial-contract tie-in and CRS-compliant beneficial owner declarations. The SCSp may interoperate with platform payment providers (Stripe) for card acceptance; for B2B settlement, maintain a main concentration account at a Luxembourg bank and settle via regular reconciliation rather than direct platform settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Euro/USD deliverable foreign-exchange forward contracts for hedging import costs and export revenues.
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts for emerging-market currencies (e.g., CNY, PLN, TRY) where no onshore/liquid deliverable forward exists.
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) to convert the cash-flow currency profile of the aligner sheet sales into the company's functional currency (EUR).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs – RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, within one month of the anniversary of the initial RBE registration; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days of the change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal penalties for directors and managers: imprisonment from 6 months to 5 years and/or fines up to EUR 1,250,000 for legal persons; persistent non-compliance may trigger administrative strike-off from the commercial register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS Maintenance Declaration (Declaration annuelle de maintien au registre)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, by 31 March of the following calendar year (for data as at 31 December).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties up to EUR 2,000; repeated default exposes the entity to administrative fines and potential administrative strike-off after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Annual Accounts (for SCSp exceeding statutory size thresholds)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS e-file portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the financial year-end (e.g., by 30 September for a 31 December year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fines increased monthly up to EUR 2,000; failure exceeding six months can result in criminal liability for managers and administrative strike-off from the RCS.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit required when an SCSp exceeds two of three thresholds at year-end: total balance sheet > EUR 4.4 million; net turnover > EUR 8.8 million; average employee count > 50. Below thresholds, audit is exempt.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002, as amended) implementing EU Accounting Directives; IFRS may be used voluntarily or for consolidated financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each SCSp must maintain a comprehensive RBE register and file an annual confirmation of accuracy via the LBR online portal. The confirmation is due within one month of the anniversary of the initial RBE declaration. Any transfer of partnership interests or change in beneficial ownership must be reported to the RBE within 30 days; the annual confirmation protocol requires the SCSp to review and update the register accordingly.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (including general and limited partners and their contributions)
Register of Managers (gérants) with appointment and revocation details
Minute Book (minutes of partner meetings and managerial resolutions)
Register of Encumbrances or Usufruct over partnership interests (if applicable)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 1,300 – 3,200 (EUR 1,200 – 3,000) per year for a standard registered office or administrative agent in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 5,400 – 16,200 (EUR 5,000 – 15,000) for a typical SME audit engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (aggregate of 17% corporate income tax, 7% solidarity surcharge on corporate income tax, and 6.75% municipal business tax for Luxembourg City); the SCSp itself is fiscally transparent and is not subject to entity-level corporate income tax on its profits
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp level: no statutory tax holiday and no entity-level CIT incentives because profits flow through to partners; qualifying IP income owned through the SCSp may benefit on a partner-by-partner basis from the Luxembourg IP regime (80% exemption, resulting in an effective tax rate of approximately 5.0% for corporate investors subject to the full 24.94% headline rate)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 510 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités et impôt commercial communal); electronically filed through the Administration des contributions directes eSpace via MyGuichet.lu
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within five months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year SCSp the return must be filed by 31 May of the following year, unless an extension is formally granted

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp legal name, legal form code, Luxembourg RCS registration number, and LuxTrust authentication data of the entity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Luxembourg RCS number and the registered office address; non-resident commercial partners must separately indicate their tax identification number and country of tax residence on the partner annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the accounting period for which the return is made
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the fiscal year adopted in the partnership agreement; non-calendar fiscal years may be accepted where justified by international business requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net result before tax adjustments, including gross margin, operating expenses, and depreciation related to thermoforming and automated trimming of multilayer dental aligner sheets
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the Luxembourg-source commercial profit attributable to the SCSp; partner withdrawals and capital repayments are not deductible expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary differences, disallowed expenses, tax depreciation recalculations, and any upward adjustment under Article 164(3) LIR for non-arm's-length intercompany transactions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must disclose their pro-rata share and coordinate home-jurisdiction attribution of any Luxembourg permanent establishment arising from the manufacturing activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Qualifying net income from patents, software, and eligible IP rights after applying the 80% exemption and the OECD-compatible nexus ratio
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No entity-level IP box claim is possible; each eligible partner claiming the exemption must maintain underlying qualifying IP documentation and nexus records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Set-off of tax losses brought forward from prior years after applying the applicable anti-abuse limitations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Luxembourg loss relief is computed at the partner level for a transparent SCSp; consult domestic CFC, controlled-foreign-entity, and transparency rules before recognising the deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Trade income and capital base after applying the commercial-activity assessment; taxable where the SCSp carries on production, warehousing, or logistics in Luxembourg
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An SCSp maintaining a Luxembourg establishment for dental aligner manufacturing is subject to municipal business tax; non-resident partners may be jointly assessed where the SCSp has a permanent establishment in Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Flag for separate net wealth tax return Form 540; taxable net wealth is assessed on the basis of the SCSp's Luxembourg situs assets and provisions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Review the net wealth tax exemption for undertakings held by tax-resident corporate partners and ensure economic substance conditions and art. 525 LIR requirements are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer Pricing Master File/Local File summary, country-by-country report notification references, and confirmation that contemporaneous documentation is available
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the consolidated group exceeds the relevant turnover thresholds, file Form 950 (CbCR notification) and attach detailed intercompany agreements for toll manufacturing, distribution, and IP licensing of clear aligner products.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing enables the Luxembourg tax administration to issue a default assessment; late payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month; surcharges may reach 10% of the assessed tax; wilful non-filing or false filing exposes managers to criminal fines and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for distributions made by an SCSp to its partners because the partnership is fiscally transparent and profit distribution is treated as a withdrawal of contributed capital; by contrast, the ordinary Luxembourg statutory dividend withholding tax rate is 15% for dividends paid by a Luxembourg resident company, reducible to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (holding of at least 10% of capital for 12 months) or an applicable double taxation agreement
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No dividend withholding tax is mechanically levied at the SCSp level, so no Form 166 withholding reclaim is needed for partnership distributions; for underlying Luxembourg companies held through the SCSp, the paying company must obtain from the non-resident ultimate beneficial owner a valid tax residence certificate (TRC), a completed Form 166 (or applicable reduced-withholding declaration), and, where a DTA is invoked, a beneficial-ownership self-certification; the TRC must be issued by the residence state and be valid for the calendar year of payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic withholding tax on interest is 0%; domestic withholding tax on royalties is 0%. Under double taxation agreements, royalty and interest rates typically range from 0% to 15%, subject to beneficial ownership and anti-abuse rules under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive, MLI, and ATAD; the SCSp must not be used as a conduit if the ultimate recipient lacks economic substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 of consolidated group annual turnover (alternative mandatory Master File/Local File triggers: total balance sheet exceeding EUR 43,000,000 or 250 employees); Country-by-Country Report threshold: EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain generic Economic Substance Regulations of the type seen in zero-tax offshore centres; substance is enforced through the Luxembourg General Anti-Abuse Rule, ATAD/MLI anti-abuse provisions, the substance requirements in Circular L.I.R. 164/2 for tax rulings, and the jurisdiction's administrative practice requiring real premises, staff, local decision-making, and physical operations for any commercial activity. An SCSp manufacturing dental clear aligner sheets must maintain a genuine Luxembourg establishment and cannot rely on a registered address alone to claim treaty benefits or tax transparency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion / fraudulent mispricing under LIR Article 164(3)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately charging non-arm's-length prices for toll manufacturing, distribution, or clearance of dental clear aligner sheets to shift Luxembourg taxable profit to a zero-tax or low-tax jurisdiction
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment at fair market value, late payment interest, administrative fines of up to 50% of evaded tax, and criminal prosecution for fiscal fraud carrying fines from EUR 25,000 to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing partners and directors who signed false returns or knowingly approved mispriced transfers are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and penalties; personal travel bans, asset freezes, and imprisonment of up to five years may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / artificial lack of substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp as a letterbox vehicle with no actual staff, premises, bank account, or business decision-making in Luxembourg while using the Luxembourg address to claim tax-transparency or treaty benefits for dental aligner revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the entity under GAAR and ATAD, retroactive denial of treaty benefits, loss of loss-carryforward relief, rescission of any tax ruling, and a non-compliance penalty of up to 25% of the adjusted tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners may be held personally liable for the entire tax shortfall; they may also face management disqualification, inclusion in DAC6/LuxLeaks cross-border arrangement disclosures, and travel restrictions pending resolution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / KYC breaches on payment rails (Stripe, platform credit cards)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing dental aligner payments or partnership contributions via Stripe or platform credit cards without implementing adequate AML/KYC controls, failing to file the Luxembourg beneficial-ownership register (RBE) declaration, or conducting payments beyond ancillary services without a Luxembourg payment institution licence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 1,250,000, criminal penalties of up to 10 years imprisonment for money laundering, RBE non-disclosure fines, forced closure of payment accounts, and revocation of any commercial licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and AML compliance officers are personally liable for breaches; they may face civil restitution to investors, travel bans, five-year management disqualification, and seizure of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare and maintain Master File, Local File, or Country-by-Country Report, or refusing to deliver the documentation to the Luxembourg tax administration after a formal notice with 30 days' response time
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CbCR non-filing penalty up to EUR 250,000 or €2,500 per month of delay; daily default fines; estimation of taxable income by the administration; 10% surcharge on the resulting tax assessment; criminal proceedings for wilful obstruction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general managers are jointly and severally liable for the penalties and the default assessment; tax evasion indictments may result in travel restrictions, personal asset seizure, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Disguised dividend / excessive management fee repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repatriating profits from the SCSp to non-resident partners through purported management fees, service charges, intercompany royalties, or artificially inflated subcontracting costs that have no actual business content and are not priced on an arm's-length basis
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization as taxable partnership profit or deemed dividend; recapture of Luxembourg municipal business tax; potential 15% withholding tax where recharacterised as a Luxembourg-source dividend; interest and penalties up to 10%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Partners and directors who authorised the sham payments must personally restore the withholding tax shortfall; they face asset seizure, foreign tax authority notifications, travel bans, and, in serious cases, imprisonment for tax fraud.
